facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: audited FY2025 statements, three sets of unaudited 2026 statements and three releases support a reported financial foundation, a FY2025 to Q3 2026 bridge and a last-twelve-months view. The Q3 ER shows the issuer's own last-twelve-months construction at [Q3 ER] page:15. - Strongest contrary evidence: the covenant and the leverage ratio are summarized, not supplied in the governing document. [10-K] page:183 "the Credit Agreement requires compliance with a maximum leverage ratio covenant, tested quarterly, of 5.00:1.00 through December 31, 2028" and [Q3 ER] page:16 "Maximum leverage ratio permitted under the Credit Agreement". The measure that applies is "Consolidated EBITDA" with "pro forma adjustments", which the releases say are "determined according to specified criteria set forth in the Applicable Credit Agreement" ([Q3 ER] page:15). The credit agreement and the amendment are exhibits that are not supplied. - Source risk mechanism: the covenant ratio uses funded debt less unrestricted cash over a credit-agreement EBITDA, a different construction from operating income or reported EBITDA. A consumer that equates the release's ratio with a GAAP-based ratio would misread headroom. The release states this itself: [Q3 ER] page:15 "should not be considered a substitute for the ratio of total debt to operating income". - Debt-like claims outside the debt table: operating lease liabilities appear on the balance sheet ([Q3 10-Q] page:3 "Long-term operating lease liabilities"), puttable noncontrolling interests ([Q3 10-Q] page:3), the Berkshire repurchase obligation ([Q3 10-Q] page:19) and letters of credit under a separate facility ([Q3 10-Q] page:14 "letters of credit of approximately"). The 10-K contractual obligations table ([10-K] page:135) lists leases and puts separately from "Long-term debt". CP-2 must decide inclusion explicitly. - Floating-rate exposure: the debt note describes interest rate caps with strikes and maturities ([Q3 10-Q] page:12 to page:13). The balance of floating debt not covered by caps is stated at [Q3 10-Q] page:12 "The remaining $814,456 outstanding principal balance of Term Loan A-2 and $80,000 balance outstanding on the revolving line of credit are subject to SOFR-based interest rate volatility." - What cannot proceed: verification of covenant definitions and headroom against the credit agreement, guarantor-level analysis, intercreditor or security-package analysis, ratings-based or market-based work. - Next evidence action: supply the Credit Agreement and its amendments, the indentures for each senior note series, Exhibit 21.1, the Berkshire share repurchase agreement and any filings dated October 30, 2026 to November 5, 2026.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported base shows a large, steady-earning dialysis business that has been adding debt while it returns cash to shareholders. At September 30, 2026 total debt principal is 10,832.2 (including 151.6 of finance leases and before 63.1 of unamortised discount and financing costs); cash and cash equivalents are 495.6, so net debt on the company's own definition is 10,337. Against the company's credit-agreement EBITDA of 3,042 (last twelve months, issuer non-GAAP), total debt is 3.56x and the covenant-basis net leverage is 3.38x, up from 3.26x at December 31, 2025. The statements themselves print no EBITDA: operating income plus depreciation and amortization plus the Q3 2026 impairment is 2,880.9 for the last twelve months, which gives 3.76x on total debt, a stricter reading that is shown as a sensitivity. Operating lease liabilities of 2,623.3 and noncontrolling interests subject to put provisions of 1,484.3 sit outside the debt figure. The business grew in 9M 2026 (revenue and operating income each about 5.2% above 9M 2025), but operating cash flow was 1.2% lower, free cash flow on the company definition was 672 against 716, and 870.2 went to share repurchases. Liquidity is cash of 495.6 plus 1,420.0 of undrawn revolver, down from 2,176.4 at FY2025. About 77% of debt matures in 2030 and 2031. The only financial maintenance test summarised in the filings is a maximum leverage ratio of 5.00:1.00; the company reports 3.38x, but the agreement and the definition of Consolidated EBITDA are not supplied, so headroom is a company-basis figure.

facts.label: Leases and other claims outside debt
facts.text: - Operating leases: current and long-term operating lease liabilities total 2,623.3 at September 30, 2026 ([Q3 10-Q] page:3) and 2,601.1 at December 31, 2025, with undiscounted future minimum payments of 3,001.1 ([10-K] page:188). They are outside total debt principal. The Consolidated EBITDA reconciliation shows no add-back of lease cost, so the EBITDA figures above are after operating lease cost (fixed lease expense 570.3 and variable 131.9 in FY2025, [10-K] page:187 to page:188), and adding the liabilities to debt without adding rent back would mix bases; lease-adjusted leverage is therefore not calculated (Q3 2026 LTM operating lease cost is not printed in the 10-Qs). - Finance leases: 151.6 at September 30, 2026, already inside total debt ([Q3 10-Q] page:11). - Puttable noncontrolling interests: 1,484.3 on the balance sheet at September 30, 2026 ([Q3 10-Q] page:3). facts.label: Interpretation: data to risk to credit implication
facts.text: - Leverage: the company's covenant-basis leverage rose from 3.26x at FY2025 to 3.38x at Q3 2026 while Consolidated EBITDA rose from 2,960 to 3,042; net debt grew faster than EBITDA because total debt principal rose 487.7 while cash fell 180.8. Credit implication: leverage is moving toward the top of the 3.0x to 3.5x range the 10-K says it held throughout 2025 ([10-K] page:114; the sources print no 2026 target), and it remains 1.62x inside the maximum on company figures. - Earnings: 9M 2026 revenue and operating income were each about 5.2% higher than 9M 2025, and adjusted operating income was about 7.6% higher (1,622 against 1,508). Q3 2026 operating income of 499.3 was below Q3 2025's 505.8 because of the 62.2 impairment; adjusted operating income was 561 against 579 in Q2 2026. The release attributes year-to-date cost growth to compensation, medical supplies, insurance and health benefits ([Q3 ER] page:2). Credit implication: the earnings base is growing but cost pressure is visible per treatment (patient care costs per treatment 279.24 against 271.23). - Cash conversion and capital allocation: operating cash flow for 9M 2026 was 1,329.7 against 1,345.8, and company free cash flow was 672 against 716. Cash share repurchases of 870.2 equalled about 97% of operating cash flow less additions of 898.4 and were accompanied by net debt issuance of 490 ([Q3 10-Q] page:44). Credit implication: free cash flow is directed to equity holders and the balance sheet absorbs the difference, so deleveraging depends on a change in policy. The 2026 guidance of 1,000 to 1,250 of free cash flow implies 328 to 578 for Q4 2026 (calculated). - Noncontrolling interests: the company consolidates partnerships; noncontrolling interests earned 201.8 in 9M 2026 and received distributions of 243.8, and Consolidated EBITDA adds this income back. Credit implication: part of consolidated EBITDA is cash that leaves to minority partners, so debt-to-EBITDA may understate leverage on the parent's attributable cash flow; this is not quantified here. - Liquidity and maturities: cash plus undrawn revolver was 1,915.6 at September 30, 2026 against 2,176.4 at December 31, 2025 (calculated); the revolver is nearly undrawn. Maturities before 2030 are small (31.4, 113.0, 160.4 and 146.9 in Q4 2026 to 2029), then 4,570.3 in 2030 and 3,765.1 in 2031. The Term Loan A-2 and revolver (2,042.5 drawn) fall due March 2, 2030 if the 4.625% notes are not refinanced by then. Credit implication: refinancing risk is back-ended but large and clustered, and the springing date pulls secured bank maturities forward. - Rate risk: 894.5 of floating debt is unhedged by the printed caps, whose strikes step up to 4.75% and 5.25% in later years. Credit implication: a SOFR rise has a bounded effect today but the protection is thinner after 2028. - Quality of the evidence: FY2025 statements are audited, with an unqualified opinion dated February 11, 2026 ([10-K] page:148). The quarterly statements are unaudited. Consolidated EBITDA, adjusted operating income, free cash flow and net debt are management non-GAAP presentations. The statements print no cash interest for interim periods.

rows.label: Covenant-basis net leverage is 3.38x, up from 3.26x at FY2025, against a 5.00x maximum. Earnings are growing, but buybacks and a heavy 2030 and 2031 maturity wall absorb cash flow.
Total debt rose to 10,832.2 at Q3 2026 from 10,344.6 at FY2025, while cash fell to 495.6 from 676.4.
Revenue of 10,547.8 and operating income of 1,560.1 for 9M 2026 were each about 5.2% above 9M 2025.
Share repurchases of 870.2 in 9M 2026 nearly matched operating cash flow less capital expenditure of 898.4, and net debt issuance was 490.
Debt maturing in 2030 is 4,570.3 and in 2031 is 3,765.1, about 77% of the total.
Reported leverage of 3.38x compares with a 5.00x maximum, leaving 1.62x of headroom on company figures.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: DaVita Inc. is a listed, widely held provider of dialysis and related kidney care, with no private-equity sponsor and no pending acquisition or sale of the company described in the sources. The business is dominated by U.S. outpatient dialysis, a life-sustaining, recurring therapy paid mainly by Medicare and Medicare Advantage at about 57.7% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenue and by commercial insurers at about 31.9%, with the commercial segment generating nearly all profit. That makes earnings sensitive to commercial mix and to Medicare rate setting rather than to discretionary demand. In 9M 2026 volume was steady (treatments up 0.5%) and revenue per treatment rose, but patient care costs per treatment rose faster, and the integrated kidney care and international businesses are small and volatile. Ownership is public with a significant but capped holder, Berkshire Hathaway, whose position is managed through a repurchase agreement and a standstill; the company does not pay cash dividends and has returned capital through repurchases. The only transactions in the period are financing amendments, a 200.0 minority investment in Elara Caring, share repurchases and the settlement of the Berkshire repurchase obligation. For a creditor the central mechanics are therefore operating (reimbursement, commercial mix, labor and supply cost, litigation and policy risk) and capital allocation (buybacks funded partly by net debt issuance, per the financial base), not sponsor or merger risk. The sources give no governing debt documents, so control and priming risk can be judged only from documented actions, and none of a creditor-adverse kind was found.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: There is no sponsor transaction, merger or sale of the company in the sources, and the 10-Qs list no pending business combination of that kind. The period contains these completed financing and capital events. On November 24, 2025 the Eighth Amendment to the credit agreement refinanced the revolver and Term Loan A-1 into a new revolver and Term Loan A-2 ([10-K] page:181). On June 8, 2026 the Ninth Amendment added an incremental 500.0 of Term Loan B-2 and the proceeds repaid part of the revolver, at a cost of 2.0 of extinguishment and modification costs ([Q3 10-Q] page:12). The most recent new senior notes were the 6.75% Senior Notes due 2033, issued May 23, 2025 at 1,000.0 ([10-K] page:184); no senior notes were issued in 2026 in the sources. Net debt issuance was 490 in 9M 2026 ([Q3 10-Q] page:44). The use of proceeds of the June 2026 incremental was repayment of part of the revolver and related interest and fees; the sources read state no use of proceeds for the 6.75% notes and give no single sources-and-uses table.

facts.text: Non-debt capital events: the company signed an agreement on February 2, 2026 to buy a noncontrolling minority interest in Elara Caring for approximately 200.0, which closed effective July 20, 2026 with a 200.0 cash payment subject to post-closing adjustments ([Q1 10-Q] page:17; [Q3 10-Q] page:10). The Berkshire repurchase obligation of 199.9 at December 31, 2025 was settled on January 29, 2026, and the 54.7 obligation at September 30, 2026 was settled on October 27, 2026 for 69.0 ([10-K] page:201; [Q3 10-Q] page:19). The status of each is complete; the effect on liquidity is the cash outflow and, for the revolver, the drawn balance of 80.0 at September 30, 2026 (CP-1). Between October 1 and October 27, 2026 the company repurchased a further 0.5 million shares for 87 ([Q3 ER] page:2), a subsequent event relative to the Q3 10-Q period. No change of control, delisting or deregistration is described. Creditor-relevant change-of-control terms exist in the notes (the 6.75% notes carry a 101% repurchase offer on certain change of control events, [10-K] page:184), but the indentures and credit agreement are not supplied, so their full terms are Insufficient Information.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: DaVita Inc. is a stable but increasingly shareholder-oriented credit: leverage is moderate and covenant headroom wide, yet leverage is rising because buybacks outrun free cash flow. The strongest support is recurring dialysis demand, with U.S. dialysis earning 97.3% of segment margin, USD 1,915.6 million of cash and undrawn revolver, and no year of scheduled principal above USD 160.4 million until 2030. The weakest point is capital allocation: USD 870.2 million of buybacks in nine months 2026 exceeded free cash flow of USD 672 million while covenant-basis leverage rose to 3.38x from 3.26x, and 77% of debt falls due in 2030 and 2031. What decides the outcome is commercial payor mix and Medicare rates, and whether management keeps leverage inside its range.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, DaVita Inc. earns its profit in one place. U.S. dialysis produced USD 1,588.1 million of USD 1,632.4 million of segment operating margin in nine months 2026, or 97.3%, and non-hospital commercial payors are 26% of U.S. dialysis revenue and 11% of patients but generate nearly all profit [CP-1A]. Revenue visibility is high because dialysis is recurring, but price is set by Medicare and by negotiated commercial rates, so a shift in commercial mix moves earnings sharply. Revenue per treatment rose 2.7% in nine months 2026 while patient care costs per treatment rose 3.0%, and the share of commercial revenue slipped to 31.9% from 32.5% (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

facts.text: Second, leverage is moderate but rising. Total debt principal was USD 10,832.2 million at September 30, 2026, up USD 487.7 million from December 31, 2025, while cash and cash equivalents fell to USD 495.6 million from USD 676.4 million [CP-1]. Covenant-basis net leverage rose to 3.38x from 3.26x on Consolidated EBITDA of USD 3,042 million, and total debt over that EBITDA is 3.56x. The 10-K says leverage stayed within a 3.0x to 3.5x target range throughout 2025 and prints no 2026 target [CP-1A]. On a stricter EBITDA of operating income plus depreciation and amortization plus impairment (USD 2,880.9 million) total debt is 3.76x. Debt expense over the last twelve months was USD 593.7 million, and Consolidated EBITDA over it is 5.12x (expense basis, because interim cash interest is not printed).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, DaVita Inc. returns more cash to shareholders than it keeps. Share repurchases cost USD 870.2 million in nine months 2026 against company free cash flow of USD 672 million and operating cash flow less capital additions of USD 898.4 million, which means buybacks absorbed 96.9% of the latter, and net debt issuance was USD 490 million [CP-1]. Free cash flow after buybacks was therefore negative USD 198.2 million for the period (calculated). Total equity is a deficit of USD 358.5 million. The company pays no cash dividend, the Board has authorised USD 4,000 million of repurchases in two steps since September 2024, and about USD 1,212 million remained available at October 27, 2026 [CP-1A; Q3 10-Q page:19]. The credit facilities restrict repurchases, but many of those limits fall away while leverage is below 4.00x, which it is at 3.38x (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.text: Strengths. (1) Recurring, non-discretionary demand and scale: 3,269 centers and about 298,100 patients, with U.S. dialysis 84.9% of segment revenue and 97.3% of segment margin, and no commercial payor above 10% of U.S. dialysis revenue (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (2) Adequate liquidity: USD 1,915.6 million of cash and undrawn revolver with no facility expiring within twelve months of the as-of date (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (3) Light near-term maturities: scheduled principal of USD 31.4 million, USD 113.0 million, USD 160.4 million and USD 146.9 million for the rest of 2026 through 2029, with the first final maturity in 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (4) Wide company-basis covenant headroom of 1.62x and a 0.62x margin below the 4.00x restriction-relief level (Analyst Interpretation on company figures; CP-1). (5) Low maintenance capital intensity: maintenance and development capital expenditure of USD 431 million against depreciation and amortization of USD 510.8 million in nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (6) Transparent leverage disclosure each quarter, an audited FY2025 with an unqualified opinion, and no creditor-adverse transaction found in the documented history (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information; CP-1A).

(2) Profit concentration: one segment earns 97.3% of segment margin and commercial payors generate nearly all profit while commercial revenue grew only 1.2% against 4.0% for Medicare and Medicare Advantage (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A). (3) Unit-margin squeeze: patient care costs per treatment up 3.0% against revenue per treatment up 2.7%, with wage, supply and insurance inflation and union organizing (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (4) Back-ended, repricing maturity wall: 77% of debt in 2030 and 2031, a springing March 2, 2030 date for USD 2,042.5 million of bank debt, and low-coupon notes that would refinance at higher rates (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (5) Cash leakage to minority partners and puttable interests of USD 1,484.3 million (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (6) Unverified definitions: Consolidated EBITDA and the covenant ratio are company-computed, and cash interest cover exists only for FY2025 (Insufficient Information; CP-1). (7) Regulatory, litigation and policy exposure with no quantified downside (Insufficient Information; CP-1A).

rows.label: DaVita is a stable, cash-generative credit whose leverage is rising because buybacks exceed free cash flow. Covenant-basis leverage is 3.38x against a 5.00x maximum, and liquidity is adequate. Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2030 and 2031.
Liquidity was USD 1,915.6 million at Q3 2026, cash plus undrawn revolver, down from USD 2,176.4 million at FY2025.
Buybacks of USD 870.2 million in nine months 2026 exceeded free cash flow of USD 672 million, and total debt rose to USD 10,832.2 million.
Debt maturing in 2030 and 2031 is USD 8,335.4 million, 77% of the total, and notes there carry coupons of 4.625% and 3.75%.
Covenant-basis leverage of 3.38x leaves 1.62x of headroom to the 5.00x maximum on company figures.
U.S. dialysis earned 97.3% of segment margin, and commercial payors, 26% of U.S. dialysis revenue, generate nearly all profit.

Fundamental view: a large, recurring-revenue dialysis business with moderate leverage and adequate liquidity, offset by rising leverage from buybacks, falling unit margin, commercial-payor profit concentration and a heavy 2030 to 2031 maturity wall. Not a rating and not a recommendation.

- Family and authority: issuer press releases furnished as Exhibit 99.1, management-prepared and unaudited. [Q1 ER] page:1 "Denver, Colorado, May 5, 2026"; [Q2 ER] page:1 "Denver, Colorado, August 4, 2026"; [Q3 ER] page:1 "Denver, Colorado, October 29, 2026".

- Credit agreement versions: [Q1 ER] page:15 "Under our amended senior secured credit facilities (the Amended Credit Agreement) dated November 24, 2025"; [Q2 ER] page:15 "dated June 8, 2026 and our prior senior secured credit facilities"; [Q3 ER] page:15 "dated June 8, 2026". - All sources are dated on or before October 29, 2026: the 10-K on February 11, 2026, the Q1 documents on May 5, 2026, the Q2 documents on August 4, 2026 and the Q3 documents on October 29, 2026. All precede the cutoff of 2026-11-05.

### Identity and perimeter
- Reporting entity: DAVITA INC., Delaware, NYSE ticker DVA ([10-K] page:1 "DAVITA INC. (Exact name of registrant as specified in charter)").

- Borrower and issuer: the senior secured credit facilities and senior notes are obligations of DaVita Inc. - Guarantors: the supplied text does not name the subsidiary guarantors, and no guarantor or non-guarantor financial information is supplied. The context leaves borrower, parent and guarantor fields blank, which is not evidence of their absence.

- Non-wholly-owned perimeter: the consolidated statements include noncontrolling interests. [Q3 10-Q] page:3 "Noncontrolling interests subject to put provisions" sits between liabilities and equity on the balance sheet, and [Q3 ER] page:15 shows "Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests" as an add-back in Consolidated EBITDA. Statement figures are consolidated, not attributable to DaVita Inc. alone, unless a line says otherwise.

| Consumer | Evidence it needs | Located | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, debt, liquidity, cash flow, non-GAAP | [10-K] page:153 to page:155, page:178 to page:184; [Q3 10-Q] page:2 to page:4, page:11 to page:14, page:44 to page:47; [Q3 ER] page:9 to page:16 | Unit mix; non-GAAP figures are issuer-computed; Q1 10-Q has no maturity schedule |

| CP-2 | CP-1 and CP-1A outputs; maturities; covenant summary; liquidity; caps; leverage | [10-K] page:135, page:183 to page:184; [Q3 10-Q] page:12 to page:14, page:47; [Q3 ER] page:15 to page:16 | Executed agreements not supplied; Consolidated EBITDA definition and add-backs unverifiable |
| CP-5 | Traceable claims | All seven sources carry page locators | HTML and XBRL not supplied; extraction fidelity not reviewed |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: audited FY2025 statements, three sets of unaudited 2026 statements and three releases support a reported financial foundation, a FY2025 to Q3 2026 bridge and a last-twelve-months view. The Q3 ER shows the issuer's own last-twelve-months construction at [Q3 ER] page:15.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the covenant and the leverage ratio are summarized, not supplied in the governing document. [10-K] page:183 "the Credit Agreement requires compliance with a maximum leverage ratio covenant, tested quarterly, of 5.00:1.00 through December 31, 2028" and [Q3 ER] page:16 "Maximum leverage ratio permitted under the Credit Agreement". The measure that applies is "Consolidated EBITDA" with "pro forma adjustments", which the releases say are "determined according to specified criteria set forth in the Applicable Credit Agreement" ([Q3 ER] page:15). The credit agreement and the amendment are exhibits that are not supplied.

- Source risk mechanism: the covenant ratio uses funded debt less unrestricted cash over a credit-agreement EBITDA, a different construction from operating income or reported EBITDA. A consumer that equates the release's ratio with a GAAP-based ratio would misread headroom. The release states this itself: [Q3 ER] page:15 "should not be considered a substitute for the ratio of total debt to operating income".

- Debt-like claims outside the debt table: operating lease liabilities appear on the balance sheet ([Q3 10-Q] page:3 "Long-term operating lease liabilities"), puttable noncontrolling interests ([Q3 10-Q] page:3), the Berkshire repurchase obligation ([Q3 10-Q] page:19) and letters of credit under a separate facility ([Q3 10-Q] page:14 "letters of credit of approximately"). The 10-K contractual obligations table ([10-K] page:135) lists leases and puts separately from "Long-term debt". CP-2 must decide inclusion explicitly.

- Floating-rate exposure: the debt note describes interest rate caps with strikes and maturities ([Q3 10-Q] page:12 to page:13). The balance of floating debt not covered by caps is stated at [Q3 10-Q] page:12 "The remaining $814,456 outstanding principal balance of Term Loan A-2 and $80,000 balance outstanding on the revolving line of credit are subject to SOFR-based interest rate volatility."

- What cannot proceed: verification of covenant definitions and headroom against the credit agreement, guarantor-level analysis, intercreditor or security-package analysis, ratings-based or market-based work.

- Next evidence action: supply the Credit Agreement and its amendments, the indentures for each senior note series, Exhibit 21.1, the Berkshire share repurchase agreement and any filings dated October 30, 2026 to November 5, 2026.

| Text extraction only; filed HTML and XBRL not compared; no images or charts inspected | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Check flagged tables against the filed HTML when available |
## Next module

- CP-1: use the 10-K and 10-Q statements as controlling; keep quarter, nine-month, last-twelve-month and FY2025 figures apart; convert thousands and millions explicitly; label adjusted figures, free cash flow, Consolidated EBITDA and the leverage ratio as issuer non-GAAP.

### Financial base view

The reported base shows a large, steady-earning dialysis business that has been adding debt while it returns cash to shareholders. At September 30, 2026 total debt principal is 10,832.2 (including 151.6 of finance leases and before 63.1 of unamortised discount and financing costs); cash and cash equivalents are 495.6, so net debt on the company's own definition is 10,337. Against the company's credit-agreement EBITDA of 3,042 (last twelve months, issuer non-GAAP), total debt is 3.56x and the covenant-basis net leverage is 3.38x, up from 3.26x at December 31, 2025. The statements themselves print no EBITDA: operating income plus depreciation and amortization plus the Q3 2026 impairment is 2,880.9 for the last twelve months, which gives 3.76x on total debt, a stricter reading that is shown as a sensitivity. Operating lease liabilities of 2,623.3 and noncontrolling interests subject to put provisions of 1,484.3 sit outside the debt figure. The business grew in 9M 2026 (revenue and operating income each about 5.2% above 9M 2025), but operating cash flow was 1.2% lower, free cash flow on the company definition was 672 against 716, and 870.2 went to share repurchases. Liquidity is cash of 495.6 plus 1,420.0 of undrawn revolver, down from 2,176.4 at FY2025. About 77% of debt matures in 2030 and 2031. The only financial maintenance test summarised in the filings is a maximum leverage ratio of 5.00:1.00; the company reports 3.38x, but the agreement and the definition of Consolidated EBITDA are not supplied, so headroom is a company-basis figure.

The Ninth Amendment of June 8, 2026 added an incremental 500.0 to Term Loan B-2, with proceeds used to repay part of the revolver, and cost 2.0 of debt extinguishment and modification costs in Q2 2026 ([Q3 10-Q] page:12). Revolver draws were 375.0 at March 31, 2026, 65.0 at June 30, 2026 and 80.0 at September 30, 2026.

- Impairment: Q3 2026 included a 62.2 goodwill and other asset impairment for the China reporting unit, with goodwill of 42.9 remaining and carrying amount coverage shown as nil ([Q3 10-Q] page:10 to page:11; [Q3 ER] page:2). It reduced operating income but is added back in Consolidated EBITDA and adjusted operating income.

- Acquisitions and investments: the 200.0 Elara Caring minority investment closed July 20, 2026 and is equity method ([Q3 10-Q] page:10); cash paid for acquisitions was 41.7 in 9M 2026 against 118.3 in 9M 2025.

- Capital returns: 9M 2026 repurchases were 5.8 million shares for 870.2 of cash; the company repurchased a further 0.5 million shares for 87 between October 1 and October 27, 2026, and had approximately 1,212 available under current authorizations ([Q3 ER] page:2; [Q3 10-Q] page:19). These are subsequent events relative to September 30, 2026.

- Guidance (issuer, [Q3 ER] page:3): adjusted operating income 2,175 to 2,250 (prior 2,150 to 2,250), adjusted diluted EPS 14.30 to 15.20 (prior 14.10 to 15.20) and free cash flow 1,000 to 1,250 (unchanged). Guidance is management's forward-looking statement, not evidence of results.

- Comparability: the FY2025 income statement includes 25.0 of income from discontinued operations in net income; this answer uses continuing operations for earnings rows. FY2025 included the 2025 cybersecurity incident charges. Cash paid for interest is available for FY2025 only.
- Events after September 30, 2026 up to the cutoff: share repurchases and the Berkshire settlement above, both stated as of October 27, 2026. Nothing is supplied after October 29, 2026.
### Interpretation: data to risk to credit implication

- Leverage: the company's covenant-basis leverage rose from 3.26x at FY2025 to 3.38x at Q3 2026 while Consolidated EBITDA rose from 2,960 to 3,042; net debt grew faster than EBITDA because total debt principal rose 487.7 while cash fell 180.8. Credit implication: leverage is moving toward the top of the 3.0x to 3.5x range the 10-K says it held throughout 2025 ([10-K] page:114; the sources print no 2026 target), and it remains 1.62x inside the maximum on company figures.

- Earnings: 9M 2026 revenue and operating income were each about 5.2% higher than 9M 2025, and adjusted operating income was about 7.6% higher (1,622 against 1,508). Q3 2026 operating income of 499.3 was below Q3 2025's 505.8 because of the 62.2 impairment; adjusted operating income was 561 against 579 in Q2 2026. The release attributes year-to-date cost growth to compensation, medical supplies, insurance and health benefits ([Q3 ER] page:2). Credit implication: the earnings base is growing but cost pressure is visible per treatment (patient care costs per treatment 279.24 against 271.23).

- Cash conversion and capital allocation: operating cash flow for 9M 2026 was 1,329.7 against 1,345.8, and company free cash flow was 672 against 716. Cash share repurchases of 870.2 equalled about 97% of operating cash flow less additions of 898.4 and were accompanied by net debt issuance of 490 ([Q3 10-Q] page:44). Credit implication: free cash flow is directed to equity holders and the balance sheet absorbs the difference, so deleveraging depends on a change in policy. The 2026 guidance of 1,000 to 1,250 of free cash flow implies 328 to 578 for Q4 2026 (calculated).

- Noncontrolling interests: the company consolidates partnerships; noncontrolling interests earned 201.8 in 9M 2026 and received distributions of 243.8, and Consolidated EBITDA adds this income back. Credit implication: part of consolidated EBITDA is cash that leaves to minority partners, so debt-to-EBITDA may understate leverage on the parent's attributable cash flow; this is not quantified here.

- Liquidity and maturities: cash plus undrawn revolver was 1,915.6 at September 30, 2026 against 2,176.4 at December 31, 2025 (calculated); the revolver is nearly undrawn. Maturities before 2030 are small (31.4, 113.0, 160.4 and 146.9 in Q4 2026 to 2029), then 4,570.3 in 2030 and 3,765.1 in 2031. The Term Loan A-2 and revolver (2,042.5 drawn) fall due March 2, 2030 if the 4.625% notes are not refinanced by then. Credit implication: refinancing risk is back-ended but large and clustered, and the springing date pulls secured bank maturities forward.

- Rate risk: 894.5 of floating debt is unhedged by the printed caps, whose strikes step up to 4.75% and 5.25% in later years. Credit implication: a SOFR rise has a bounded effect today but the protection is thinner after 2028.

- Quality of the evidence: FY2025 statements are audited, with an unqualified opinion dated February 11, 2026 ([10-K] page:148). The quarterly statements are unaudited. Consolidated EBITDA, adjusted operating income, free cash flow and net debt are management non-GAAP presentations. The statements print no cash interest for interim periods.
## Calculations

All inputs are US$ thousands from the cited statements, shown in millions; sums use the unrounded thousands, so a sum of rounded components can differ by 0.1. "LTM" is FY2025 plus the 2026 year-to-date amount minus the 2025 year-to-date amount of the same length.
### LTM and discrete-quarter amounts

- Operating cash flow: Q2 2026 = six months 810.9 - Q1 320.8 = 490.1; Q3 2026 = nine months 1,329.7 - six months 810.9 = 518.8; LTM = 1,886.5 + 1,329.7 - 1,345.8 = 1,870.5, which agrees with the 1,870 the Q3 release prints ([Q3 ER] page:2).
- Distributions to noncontrolling interests: Q2 = 149.9 - 85.4 = 64.5; Q3 = 243.8 - 149.9 = 93.9; LTM = 324.3 + 243.8 - 232.7 = 335.3.

- Adjusted operating income (millions): LTM = 2,094 + 1,622 - 1,508 = 2,208; quarters 482 + 579 + 561 = 1,622. Free cash flow: LTM = 1,024 + 672 - 716 = 980 (agrees with the 980 printed in [Q3 ER] page:2); quarters 140 + 256 + 276 = 672.
### Leverage and coverage

- Net debt (cash only) / Consolidated EBITDA: company net debt equals total debt less cash and cash equivalents: FY2025 10,344.6 - 676.4 = 9,668.1; Q3 10,832.2 - 495.6 = 10,336.6 (company prints 10,337). Ratios: 9,668 / 2,960 = 3.27; 10,050 / 3,008 = 3.34; 10,179 / 3,018 = 3.37; 10,337 / 3,042 = 3.40.
- Covenant-basis net leverage recomputed: 9,648 / 2,960 = 3.26; 10,031 / 3,008 = 3.34; 10,162 / 3,018 = 3.37; 10,269 / 3,042 = 3.38. All agree with the printed ratios.
### Growth, shares and other derived figures

- Growth 9M 2026 over 9M 2025: revenue 10,547.8 / 10,023.3 - 1 = 5.2%; operating income 1,560.1 / 1,482.5 - 1 = 5.2%; adjusted operating income 1,622 / 1,508 - 1 = 7.6%; operating cash flow 1,329.7 / 1,345.8 - 1 = -1.2%; company free cash flow 672 / 716 - 1 = -6.1%.

- Share repurchases relative to cash generation: 870.2 / 898.4 = 97% of operating cash flow less additions (9M 2026). Net debt issuance: borrowings 3,511.3 less payments on long-term debt 3,021.0 = 490.3 ([Q3 10-Q] page:4; printed as 490 in [Q3 10-Q] page:44).
- Springing maturity exposure: Term Loan A-2 1,962.5 + revolver 80.0 = 2,042.5.
- Unhedged floating debt: Term Loan A-2 balance subject to rate volatility 814.5 + revolver 80.0 = 894.5 (as stated in the filing).
- Liquidity: Q3 2026 cash 495.6 + undrawn revolver 1,420.0 = 1,915.6; FY2025 676.4 + 1,500.0 = 2,176.4; change -260.8. Including short-term investments: 1,986.3 at Q3 2026.
- Covenant headroom: 5.00 - 3.38 = 1.62x; EBITDA floor at constant net debt 10,269 / 5.00 = 2,053.8; cushion 3,042 - 2,053.8 = 988.2, which is 32.5% of 3,042; 4.00 - 3.38 = 0.62x.
- Guidance-implied Q4 free cash flow: 1,000 - 672 = 328 and 1,250 - 672 = 578.
- Noncontrolling share of 9M 2026 consolidated net income: 201.8 / 887.6 = 22.7%.

| Ratings, market prices and peer data not supplied | Low for this scope | CP-2 | Not required for CP-1 |
| Unit mix (thousands and millions) and issuer non-GAAP measures | Low | CP-1, CP-2 | Keep US$ millions with stated precision; label non-GAAP |

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| DaVita is a large kidney care provider with no sponsor and no pending deal. U.S. dialysis earns 97.3% of segment margin, and commercial payors drive profit. The creditor issues are reimbursement policy, unit-cost growth and buyback-led capital allocation. | Medium | No credit agreement, indenture, guarantor list, Berkshire agreement or proxy statement is supplied, and nothing after October 29, 2026 is available. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| U.S. dialysis supplied 97.3% of segment operating margin and 84.9% of segment revenue in 9M 2026. | Credit quality rests on one reimbursement-driven business, with ancillary services still small. | High |

| Non-hospital commercial payors were 26% of U.S. dialysis revenue and 11% of patients in FY2025 but generate nearly all profit. | Small shifts in commercial mix or rates move earnings; the expiry of enhanced premium tax credits already pressures mix. | High |
| Revenue per treatment rose 2.7% in 9M 2026 while patient care costs per treatment rose 3.0%. | Unit margin narrowed before any change in volume, which grew 0.5%. | Medium |

| Berkshire's stake is managed to 45.0% by a repurchase agreement and a standstill, and 9M 2026 buybacks were 5.8 million shares. | Owner influence is bounded, but capital allocation favours share repurchases over deleveraging. | Medium |
| A China impairment, open government inquiries and a new federal Kidney Care National Plan add policy and legal uncertainty. | Event risk is real but not quantified in the filings. | Low |
### Business and transaction view

DaVita Inc. is a listed, widely held provider of dialysis and related kidney care, with no private-equity sponsor and no pending acquisition or sale of the company described in the sources. The business is dominated by U.S. outpatient dialysis, a life-sustaining, recurring therapy paid mainly by Medicare and Medicare Advantage at about 57.7% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenue and by commercial insurers at about 31.9%, with the commercial segment generating nearly all profit. That makes earnings sensitive to commercial mix and to Medicare rate setting rather than to discretionary demand. In 9M 2026 volume was steady (treatments up 0.5%) and revenue per treatment rose, but patient care costs per treatment rose faster, and the integrated kidney care and international businesses are small and volatile. Ownership is public with a significant but capped holder, Berkshire Hathaway, whose position is managed through a repurchase agreement and a standstill; the company does not pay cash dividends and has returned capital through repurchases. The only transactions in the period are financing amendments, a 200.0 minority investment in Elara Caring, share repurchases and the settlement of the Berkshire repurchase obligation. For a creditor the central mechanics are therefore operating (reimbursement, commercial mix, labor and supply cost, litigation and policy risk) and capital allocation (buybacks funded partly by net debt issuance, per the financial base), not sponsor or merger risk. The sources give no governing debt documents, so control and priming risk can be judged only from documented actions, and none of a creditor-adverse kind was found.

| Scale | As of September 30, 2026 the company provided dialysis to approximately 298,100 patients at 3,269 outpatient dialysis centers, of which 2,671 were in the United States and 598 in 14 other countries. | Documentary Fact | [Q3 ER] page:3 | Network density supports payor contracting and fixed-cost absorption. |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no sponsor transaction, merger or sale of the company in the sources, and the 10-Qs list no pending business combination of that kind. The period contains these completed financing and capital events. On November 24, 2025 the Eighth Amendment to the credit agreement refinanced the revolver and Term Loan A-1 into a new revolver and Term Loan A-2 ([10-K] page:181). On June 8, 2026 the Ninth Amendment added an incremental 500.0 of Term Loan B-2 and the proceeds repaid part of the revolver, at a cost of 2.0 of extinguishment and modification costs ([Q3 10-Q] page:12). The most recent new senior notes were the 6.75% Senior Notes due 2033, issued May 23, 2025 at 1,000.0 ([10-K] page:184); no senior notes were issued in 2026 in the sources. Net debt issuance was 490 in 9M 2026 ([Q3 10-Q] page:44). The use of proceeds of the June 2026 incremental was repayment of part of the revolver and related interest and fees; the sources read state no use of proceeds for the 6.75% notes and give no single sources-and-uses table.

Non-debt capital events: the company signed an agreement on February 2, 2026 to buy a noncontrolling minority interest in Elara Caring for approximately 200.0, which closed effective July 20, 2026 with a 200.0 cash payment subject to post-closing adjustments ([Q1 10-Q] page:17; [Q3 10-Q] page:10). The Berkshire repurchase obligation of 199.9 at December 31, 2025 was settled on January 29, 2026, and the 54.7 obligation at September 30, 2026 was settled on October 27, 2026 for 69.0 ([10-K] page:201; [Q3 10-Q] page:19). The status of each is complete; the effect on liquidity is the cash outflow and, for the revolver, the drawn balance of 80.0 at September 30, 2026 (CP-1). Between October 1 and October 27, 2026 the company repurchased a further 0.5 million shares for 87 ([Q3 ER] page:2), a subsequent event relative to the Q3 10-Q period. No change of control, delisting or deregistration is described. Creditor-relevant change-of-control terms exist in the notes (the 6.75% notes carry a 101% repurchase offer on certain change of control events, [10-K] page:184), but the indentures and credit agreement are not supplied, so their full terms are Insufficient Information.

| Behaviour or fact | Evidence | Category | Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility | Locator |

| Public ownership with a capped large holder | Under the Berkshire repurchase agreement the company repurchases shares so that Berkshire's holding returns to 45.0% whenever it owns at least 45.0%; the percentage Berkshire owns today is not stated in the pages read | Documentary Fact | Capacity: contractual. Willingness: the company bought 3.1 million shares from Berkshire in 9M 2026 (419.3 of cash). Feasibility: funded from cash flow and borrowings | [10-K] page:200; [Q3 10-Q] page:18 |

| Standstill | Berkshire is bound by a standstill: "the standstill agreement requires Berkshire to vote any shares it beneficially holds in excess of 40% of the then-outstanding voting stock of the Company in accordance with the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Company (Board)" | Documentary Fact | Capacity: restricts Berkshire's control actions. It "terminates automatically if the Company enters into or publicly announces a plan to enter into a definitive agreement concerning a transaction involving all or a controlling portion of the Company's equity securities" | [10-K] page:202 |

## Calculations
All figures are US$ millions from the cited pages unless a percentage or count; sums use unrounded thousands.

- U.S. dialysis share of total net segment revenues, 9M 2026: 9,004.0 / 10,610.1 = 84.9% (ancillary 1,606.1 / 10,610.1 = 15.1%). Share of segment operating margin: 1,588.1 / 1,632.4 = 97.3%; FY2025: 2,084.2 / 2,176.6 = 95.8%; ancillary 9M 2026 share: 44.2 / 1,632.4 = 2.7%.
- Payor revenue growth, 9M 2026 over 9M 2025: Medicare and Medicare Advantage 5,180.8 / 4,983.9 - 1 = 4.0%; commercial 2,863.9 / 2,828.8 - 1 = 1.2%.
- Per-treatment growth: revenue 416.22 / 405.15 - 1 = 2.7%; patient care costs 279.24 / 271.23 - 1 = 3.0%.
- Cost ratios, 9M 2026: patient care costs 7,185.3 / 10,547.8 = 68.1%; general and administrative 1,254.1 / 10,547.8 = 11.9%.
- IKC revenue growth: 422 / 352 - 1 = 19.9%; international: 1,156 / 979 - 1 = 18.1% (both as printed rounded millions, [Q3 10-Q] page:40).
- Distributions to noncontrolling interests relative to their income: 243.8 / 201.8 = 121%.
- Berkshire repurchases in 9M 2026: 3,062 thousand shares for 419.3 ([Q3 10-Q] page:18); total repurchases 5,837 thousand shares for 862.5.

spans.text: # CP-2 — Fundamental credit synthesis: DAVITA INC. (dva)
## Request

DAVITA INC. (issuer id `dva`), as of 2026-11-05, pathway `credit_snapshot`, asks for the fundamental credit view from the upstream financial base and the business and transaction context. Scope is the consolidated company in USD millions for FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, with no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

Locators are `page:N` of the pinned `.jsonl` text of each source. Tags: [10-K] annual report, [Q1 10-Q], [Q2 10-Q], [Q3 10-Q] quarterly reports, [Q1 ER], [Q2 ER], [Q3 ER] earnings releases. This answer relies on CP-1 and CP-1A for figures and facts; it cites source pages only where it adds a fact or a calculation.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| DaVita is a stable, cash-generative credit whose leverage is rising because buybacks exceed free cash flow. Covenant-basis leverage is 3.38x against a 5.00x maximum, and liquidity is adequate. Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2030 and 2031. | Medium | The credit agreement, indentures and guarantor list are not supplied, so covenant definitions and headroom are company-reported figures that cannot be verified. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Liquidity was USD 1,915.6 million at Q3 2026, cash plus undrawn revolver, down from USD 2,176.4 million at FY2025. | Cover for scheduled principal through 2029 is ample, but the cushion narrowed. | High |

| Buybacks of USD 870.2 million in nine months 2026 exceeded free cash flow of USD 672 million, and total debt rose to USD 10,832.2 million. | Shareholder returns, not deleveraging, set the leverage path. | Medium |

| Debt maturing in 2030 and 2031 is USD 8,335.4 million, 77% of the total, and notes there carry coupons of 4.625% and 3.75%. | Refinancing at recent issue coupons would raise interest cost. | Medium |
| Covenant-basis leverage of 3.38x leaves 1.62x of headroom to the 5.00x maximum on company figures. | Headroom looks wide but the definitions cannot be verified. | Low |

| U.S. dialysis earned 97.3% of segment margin, and commercial payors, 26% of U.S. dialysis revenue, generate nearly all profit. | Earnings depend on commercial mix and Medicare rate setting. | High |
### Credit view

DaVita Inc. is a stable but increasingly shareholder-oriented credit: leverage is moderate and covenant headroom wide, yet leverage is rising because buybacks outrun free cash flow. The strongest support is recurring dialysis demand, with U.S. dialysis earning 97.3% of segment margin, USD 1,915.6 million of cash and undrawn revolver, and no year of scheduled principal above USD 160.4 million until 2030. The weakest point is capital allocation: USD 870.2 million of buybacks in nine months 2026 exceeded free cash flow of USD 672 million while covenant-basis leverage rose to 3.38x from 3.26x, and 77% of debt falls due in 2030 and 2031. What decides the outcome is commercial payor mix and Medicare rates, and whether management keeps leverage inside its range.
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental view: a large, recurring-revenue dialysis business with moderate leverage and adequate liquidity, offset by rising leverage from buybacks, falling unit margin, commercial-payor profit concentration and a heavy 2030 to 2031 maturity wall. Not a rating and not a recommendation. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium (below High because the credit agreement, indentures and guarantor list are not supplied) | CP-1 debt, liquidity, maturity and ratio figures; CP-1A segment, payor, ownership and capital-allocation rows |
### Key findings

First, DaVita Inc. earns its profit in one place. U.S. dialysis produced USD 1,588.1 million of USD 1,632.4 million of segment operating margin in nine months 2026, or 97.3%, and non-hospital commercial payors are 26% of U.S. dialysis revenue and 11% of patients but generate nearly all profit [CP-1A]. Revenue visibility is high because dialysis is recurring, but price is set by Medicare and by negotiated commercial rates, so a shift in commercial mix moves earnings sharply. Revenue per treatment rose 2.7% in nine months 2026 while patient care costs per treatment rose 3.0%, and the share of commercial revenue slipped to 31.9% from 32.5% (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

Second, leverage is moderate but rising. Total debt principal was USD 10,832.2 million at September 30, 2026, up USD 487.7 million from December 31, 2025, while cash and cash equivalents fell to USD 495.6 million from USD 676.4 million [CP-1]. Covenant-basis net leverage rose to 3.38x from 3.26x on Consolidated EBITDA of USD 3,042 million, and total debt over that EBITDA is 3.56x. The 10-K says leverage stayed within a 3.0x to 3.5x target range throughout 2025 and prints no 2026 target [CP-1A]. On a stricter EBITDA of operating income plus depreciation and amortization plus impairment (USD 2,880.9 million) total debt is 3.76x. Debt expense over the last twelve months was USD 593.7 million, and Consolidated EBITDA over it is 5.12x (expense basis, because interim cash interest is not printed).

Third, DaVita Inc. returns more cash to shareholders than it keeps. Share repurchases cost USD 870.2 million in nine months 2026 against company free cash flow of USD 672 million and operating cash flow less capital additions of USD 898.4 million, which means buybacks absorbed 96.9% of the latter, and net debt issuance was USD 490 million [CP-1]. Free cash flow after buybacks was therefore negative USD 198.2 million for the period (calculated). Total equity is a deficit of USD 358.5 million. The company pays no cash dividend, the Board has authorised USD 4,000 million of repurchases in two steps since September 2024, and about USD 1,212 million remained available at October 27, 2026 [CP-1A; Q3 10-Q page:19]. The credit facilities restrict repurchases, but many of those limits fall away while leverage is below 4.00x, which it is at 3.38x (Analyst Interpretation).

Fourth, liquidity is adequate and the near-term maturity profile is light. Cash of USD 495.6 million plus USD 1,420.0 million of undrawn revolver is USD 1,915.6 million, 4.2 times the USD 451.7 million of scheduled principal due from the rest of 2026 through 2029 (calculated). No facility expires within twelve months of the as-of date; the revolver matures November 24, 2030, or March 2, 2030 if the 4.625% senior notes are still outstanding 91 days before their maturity. That springing date puts USD 2,042.5 million of Term Loan A-2 and revolver balances in 2030 ahead of the notes' June 1, 2030 maturity [CP-1].

Fifth, refinancing is concentrated and would reprice. Maturities are USD 4,570.3 million in 2030 and USD 3,765.1 million in 2031, together USD 8,335.4 million or 77% of total debt [CP-1]. The 4.625% senior notes (USD 2,750.0 million) and 3.75% senior notes (USD 1,500.0 million) sit in that window. DaVita Inc. issued its 6.75% senior notes due 2033 in May 2025 [CP-1A]. As an illustration only, replacing those two series at 6.75% would add about USD 103.4 million of annual interest, 17.4% of last-twelve-months debt expense (calculated; not a forecast).

Sixth, covenant headroom looks wide on company figures but cannot be verified. The credit agreement sets a maximum leverage ratio of 5.00:1.00 through December 31, 2028, falling to 4.50:1.00, against a reported 3.38x, so headroom is 1.62x. At constant Consolidated net debt of USD 10,269 million, Consolidated EBITDA could fall to USD 2,053.8 million, a cushion of USD 988.2 million or 32.5%, before the 5.00x maximum; and 15.6% before the 4.00x level below which many restrictions lapse (calculated) [CP-1]. The Consolidated EBITDA definition includes pro forma adjustments, expected cost savings and other add-backs set by an agreement that is not supplied, so these cushions are company-basis (Insufficient Information on the definitions).

Seventh, claims outside the debt figure are large but different in kind. Operating lease liabilities are USD 2,623.3 million, noncontrolling interests subject to put provisions are USD 1,484.3 million, and letters of credit of about USD 184.8 million sit under a separate bilateral facility [CP-1]. Consolidated EBITDA is after lease cost, so adding the lease liability to debt would mix bases and is not done. Distributions to minority partners were USD 243.8 million in nine months 2026 against their income of USD 201.8 million, so part of consolidated EBITDA leaves the group [CP-1; CP-1A].

Eighth, interest rate and policy exposure are bounded but real. Floating-rate debt of USD 894.5 million is not covered by the interest rate caps, which hedge USD 3,500.0 million of notional through 2028 at weighted average strikes of 4.32% to 4.46%, rising to 4.75% in 2029 and 5.25% in 2030 [CP-1]. A one-point rise on the uncovered amount would cost about USD 8.9 million a year before tax (calculated). The 10-K estimates the effect of a 100 basis point rise at about USD 5.3 million of net income for 2025, net of tax and caps [10-K page:142]. Policy and legal risk is larger: a transitional drug add-on payment ends in 2026, an HHS Kidney Care National Plan was issued October 20, 2026, and False Claims Act, California Department of Insurance, District of Columbia and Federal Trade Commission matters are open with accruals described as immaterial [CP-1A]. A China impairment of USD 62.2 million in Q3 2026 shows international reimbursement risk, though international is about 10% of revenue (Documentary Fact; [10-K] page:142).
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Recurring, non-discretionary demand and scale: 3,269 centers and about 298,100 patients, with U.S. dialysis 84.9% of segment revenue and 97.3% of segment margin, and no commercial payor above 10% of U.S. dialysis revenue (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (2) Adequate liquidity: USD 1,915.6 million of cash and undrawn revolver with no facility expiring within twelve months of the as-of date (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (3) Light near-term maturities: scheduled principal of USD 31.4 million, USD 113.0 million, USD 160.4 million and USD 146.9 million for the rest of 2026 through 2029, with the first final maturity in 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (4) Wide company-basis covenant headroom of 1.62x and a 0.62x margin below the 4.00x restriction-relief level (Analyst Interpretation on company figures; CP-1). (5) Low maintenance capital intensity: maintenance and development capital expenditure of USD 431 million against depreciation and amortization of USD 510.8 million in nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (6) Transparent leverage disclosure each quarter, an audited FY2025 with an unqualified opinion, and no creditor-adverse transaction found in the documented history (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information; CP-1A).

Weaknesses. (1) Rising leverage from capital returns: buybacks of USD 870.2 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 672 million, net debt issuance was USD 490 million and total equity is a deficit (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1, CP-1A). (2) Profit concentration: one segment earns 97.3% of segment margin and commercial payors generate nearly all profit while commercial revenue grew only 1.2% against 4.0% for Medicare and Medicare Advantage (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A). (3) Unit-margin squeeze: patient care costs per treatment up 3.0% against revenue per treatment up 2.7%, with wage, supply and insurance inflation and union organizing (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (4) Back-ended, repricing maturity wall: 77% of debt in 2030 and 2031, a springing March 2, 2030 date for USD 2,042.5 million of bank debt, and low-coupon notes that would refinance at higher rates (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (5) Cash leakage to minority partners and puttable interests of USD 1,484.3 million (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (6) Unverified definitions: Consolidated EBITDA and the covenant ratio are company-computed, and cash interest cover exists only for FY2025 (Insufficient Information; CP-1). (7) Regulatory, litigation and policy exposure with no quantified downside (Insufficient Information; CP-1A).
### Debt and claims inventory
| Claim | Amount (US$m) | Date | Inside the debt figure? | Security, guarantors, maturity | Locator |
| Term Loan A-2 | 1,962.5 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior secured; guaranteed; November 24, 2030 (March 2, 2030 if 4.625% notes remain); SOFR + 1.50% | [Q3 10-Q] page:11; [10-K] page:183 |
| Term Loan B-2 | 2,352.0 | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior secured; guaranteed; May 9, 2031; SOFR + 1.75% | [Q3 10-Q] page:11 |

| Revolving line of credit (1,500.0 commitment) | 80.0 drawn | Sept 30, 2026 | Yes | Senior secured; guaranteed; November 24, 2030 (March 2, 2030 if 4.625% notes remain) | [Q3 10-Q] page:11, page:14 |

- Refinancing illustration: 2,750.0 x (6.75% - 4.625%) = 58.4; 1,500.0 x (6.75% - 3.75%) = 45.0; total 103.4; 103.4 / 593.7 (last-twelve-months debt expense) = 17.4%. Uses the 6.75% coupon of the May 2025 issue as the assumed rate; not a forecast.

- Covenant headroom: 5.00 - 3.38 = 1.62x. EBITDA floor at constant net debt: 10,269 / 5.00 = 2,053.8; cushion 3,042 - 2,053.8 = 988.2 = 32.5% of 3,042. Level 4.00x: 10,269 / 4.00 = 2,567.3; cushion 3,042 - 2,567.3 = 474.8 = 15.6%; additional net debt capacity before 4.00x at constant EBITDA: 4.00 x 3,042 - 10,269 = 1,899.0; before 5.00x: 5.00 x 3,042 - 10,269 = 4,941.0.

- Segment shares: U.S. dialysis margin 1,588.1 / 1,632.4 = 97.3%; revenue 9,004.0 / 10,610.1 = 84.9% (CP-1A).
- Minority leakage: distributions 243.8 against income 201.8, a difference of 42.0.
